## Proof

Let $f(x) \in \mathbb{Q}[x]$ be the minimal polynomial of $\theta$ over $\mathbb{Q}$. Then $\deg f = n$ and
$$K = \mathbb{Q}(\theta) \cong \mathbb{Q}[x]/(f(x)).$$

**Factorization over $\mathbb{Q}_p$.** View $f(x)$ as a polynomial over $\mathbb{Q}_p$. Since $\operatorname{char}(\mathbb{Q}_p) = 0$, the polynomial $f$ is separable, so it factors over $\mathbb{Q}_p$ into *distinct* monic irreducibles:
$$f(x) = f_1(x)\, f_2(x) \cdots f_g(x), \qquad f_i \in \mathbb{Q}_p[x] \text{ monic irreducible, pairwise coprime.}$$
Setting $n_i := \deg f_i$, we have
$$\sum_{i=1}^{g} n_i = \deg f = n. \tag{1}$$

**Determining $[K_p : \mathbb{Q}_p]$.** The element $\theta$ is algebraic over $\mathbb{Q}_p$, and its minimal polynomial over $\mathbb{Q}_p$ is the irreducible factor $f_j(x)$ of $f$ that vanishes at the particular $p$-adic image of $\theta$ (i.e., the factor corresponding to the chosen embedding $\mathbb{Q}(\theta) \hookrightarrow \overline{\mathbb{Q}_p}$). Hence
$$K_p = \mathbb{Q}_p(\theta) \cong \mathbb{Q}_p[x]/(f_j(x)),$$
and therefore
$$\boxed{[K_p : \mathbb{Q}_p] = \deg f_j = n_j.} \tag{2}$$

**Bounds and equality condition.** From (1) and the fact that every $n_i \geq 1$:
$$1 \leq [K_p : \mathbb{Q}_p] = n_j \leq n,$$
with equality $[K_p:\mathbb{Q}_p] = n$ **if and only if** $g = 1$, i.e., $f(x)$ remains irreducible over $\mathbb{Q}_p$.

**Relation to the tensor product (completions).** By the Chinese Remainder Theorem,
$$K \otimes_{\mathbb{Q}} \mathbb{Q}_p \;\cong\; \mathbb{Q}_p[x]/(f(x)) \;\cong\; \prod_{i=1}^{g} \mathbb{Q}_p[x]/(f_i(x)) \;=\; \prod_{i=1}^{g} K_{p,i},$$
where $K_{p,i} := \mathbb{Q}_p[x]/(f_i(x))$ is the completion of $K$ at the $i$-th prime of $K$ lying above $p$. The field $K_p = \mathbb{Q}_p(\theta)$ is precisely one of these completions $K_{p,j}$, and (1) gives the fundamental identity
$$\sum_{i=1}^{g} [K_{p,i} : \mathbb{Q}_p] = n. \tag{3}$$

**Conclusion.** The degree $[K_p : \mathbb{Q}_p]$ equals the degree of the irreducible factor of the minimal polynomial $f$ of $\theta$ over $\mathbb{Q}_p$ corresponding to the chosen $p$-adic embedding of $\theta$. It satisfies $1 \leq [K_p:\mathbb{Q}_p] \leq n$, with $[K_p:\mathbb{Q}_p] = n$ if and only if $f$ is irreducible over $\mathbb{Q}_p$, and the degrees of all completions of $K$ at primes above $p$ sum to $n$.
